- **Multiple Streaming Passes:** The blocking strategy reduces the need for multiple independent streaming passes over input activations (one for each of the 27 stencil offsets) by packing and gathering data locally [S1].

The claim states that the blocking strategy reduces the need for multiple independent streaming passes over input activations (one for each of the 27 stencil offsets) by packing and gathering data locally. Source [S1] explicitly identifies the 'need for several independent streaming passes over the input activations (one for each of the 27 stencil offsets)' as a reason why the straightforward paradigm underperforms. It then describes the circumvention strategy: collecting input/output index pairs for each offset, packing them contiguously in shared memory buffers, and gathering the packed buffer input from global memory. This process effectively consolidates the data access, thereby reducing the need for separate, independent streaming passes for each offset.
